newsitem.title: USA: Unemployment rises in Chattanooga, Tenn.
newsitem.headline: Unemployment rises in Chattanooga, Tenn.

text.p: Unemployment in metropolitan Chattanooga rose to its highest monthly level in nearly five years in June, exceeding both state and national averages, the Chattanooga Times reported Friday.

The Tennessee Department of Employment Security estimated that 6 percent of the Chattanooga-area work force was out of a job during the period. The city's jobless rate rose 1.2 percent, the highest level since August 1992.
In June, unemployment across Tennessee rose on a seasonally adjusted basis by four-tenths of one percent to 5.3 percent.
Nationwide, the jobless rate rose only half as much and remained at 5 percent.
Tennessee lost 8,200 manufacturing jobs over the past year, including 3,200 in apparel and 1,300 in furniture-related job.
The number of Chattanoogans on the job in June was 2,300 less this year than in 1996. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
